Key audit matter:
Valuation of goodwill
As disclosed under note 15 of the financial
statements, the Group has significant goodwill
arising from acquisition of a subsidiary company.
The goodwill is tested annually for impairment by
comparing the carrying amount of the individual
cash generating unit (CGU) to its recoverable
amount.
The determination of the recoverable amount
being the higher of the value in use and the fair
value less costs to dispose, involves significant
estimates and assumptions of unobservable
inputs such as projected cash flows, long term
growth rates and discount rate.
The methods, estimates and assumptions used
in the determination of the fair value of the
CGU are disclosed under note 15 of the financial
statements.
How our audit addressed the matter:
We assessed management’s processes and controls for
determination of the fair value of the CGU, including
the oversight from those charged with governance.
Evaluated management’s future cash flow forecasts
by comparing them to recent actual performance and
challenged the reasonableness of the approved five-
year financial budgets of the CGU.
We challenged the reasonableness of management’s
key assumptions in relation to long term growth rates
and discount rates, as detailed below:
• Long term growth rates by comparing them to
economic and industry forecasts; and
• Discount rate by assessing the cost of capital for the
company and observable market data, as well as
considering country specific factors.
Performed sensitivity analysis of the assumptions
in the goodwill calculations based on significant
assumptions.
Tested the mathematical accuracy of the computation.
Evaluated the adequacy and consistency of disclosures
in the financial statements.
